trust_decision.summary: Per-request decision at scrapy/core/downloader/handlers/s3.py:52: the transport scheme for an s3:// request is derived from request.meta['is_secure'], and after the fix it is https unless the value is literally False, so an absent, True, or non-bool falsy value yields https.

landing_point.why: Single line where the s3:// -> HTTP(S) URL scheme is chosen; the advisory names S3DownloadHandler's plaintext default and anyone reading the summary lands on this statement.

fix_sites.entry_point: Request('s3://bucket/path') dispatched by DownloadHandlers.download_request_async() for scheme 's3' -> S3DownloadHandler.download_request()

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site or O8 route exists; the nearest argument a solver could make is that the anonymous branch (no credentials, so no Authorization/X-Amz-Security-Token to leak) needs no change, which the published fix nonetheless covers on the same line.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The plaintext opt-out must keep working: meta['is_secure'] = False has to still yield http://, mirroring the documented write-side opt-out AWS_USE_SSL = False for self-hosted S3 stores. A fix that hardcodes "https" removes the only way to reach a non-TLS S3 endpoint through an s3:// request (the download handler supports no AWS_ENDPOINT_URL).

O6_input_shapes: meta['is_secure'] = False (literal bool False only) -> http
meta['is_secure'] = None / 0 / '' (falsy but not False) -> https

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An endpoint/region-aware URL builder for s3:// requests (bucket.s3.<region>.amazonaws.com, or a configured endpoint host) that chooses its own scheme.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The write-side twin S3FilesStore already accepts AWS_ENDPOINT_URL and AWS_REGION_NAME (scrapy/pipelines/files.py:159-184, docs/topics/settings.rst:445-459), so a maintainer adding the same two settings to the download handler is a natural change, and its scheme default is a second place the same rule must hold.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A separately defaulted scheme for the SigV2 signing URL (https://s3.amazonaws.com/<bucket><path>) instead of reusing the request scheme.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Signing and transport already use different hosts in this function; a maintainer making the signing endpoint configurable would plausibly introduce its own https/http default there.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A mirrored per-request secure default in S3FilesStore driven by use_ssl=self.AWS_USE_SSL, plus the S3FeedStorage boto3 client at scrapy/extensions/feedexport.py:215-223, which accepts an endpoint_url but no use_ssl.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The codebase already has the parallel concept (AWS_USE_SSL, default None -> botocore use_ssl=True, documented with an explicit False opt-out at docs/topics/media-pipeline.rst:268-273), so a shared helper or a copied default between the read and write paths is realistic.

O9_family: CWE-319 cleartext transmission of sensitive information: insecure default transport (plaintext HTTP) for signed S3 download requests

O10_build.toolchain: hatchling build backend; pytest with --reactor=asyncio; tox envs including 'botocore' (botocore>=1.13.45) and 'min-botocore'; botocore is an optional test dependency
O10_build.project_tests: tests/test_downloader_handlers.py::TestS3 and ::TestS3Anon (marked requires_botocore, pyproject.toml:270); they replace DOWNLOAD_HANDLERS['https'] with HttpDownloadHandlerMock and mock botocore.auth.formatdate, so no network or AWS credentials are needed (tests/test_downloader_handlers.py:148-201); tests/test_downloader_handlers.py:313 covers the missing-botocore path

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace the line with scheme = "https" unconditionally (or keep truthiness via meta.get('is_secure', True)), which either deletes the documented literal-False opt-out or widens it to every falsy value such as None and 0.

out_of_scope_notes: The write-side S3 paths were inspected only because they share the S3 transport concept: S3FilesStore passes use_ssl=self.AWS_USE_SSL (scrapy/pipelines/files.py:182) and S3FeedStorage builds a boto3 client (scrapy/extensions/feedexport.py:215-223); both default to botocore's use_ssl=True and are outside this advisory's download-handler scope.
